conceptual assets.information: A system-information value initialized to the configured clock frequency and writable by a bus access, on which software can depend when reading the IP's reported system information. It enters through a bus write and leaves through the system-information read response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the value is reset and stored at line 92 but can be overwritten by bus request data at line 95, allowing a write to falsify the value returned at line 168.
conceptual assets.attack: An unprivileged bus master could issue a write selecting this word and replace the reported system information, causing software to rely on a false setting (line 95).

considered, not kept.reason: The feature, memory, cache, boot and peripheral metadata is fixed by generics and constants at build time (lines 102-150), so the build-time-values rule excludes it as a conceptual asset.
The request strobe, direction and address only select and qualify accesses to the information words (lines 94 and 161-162), so they are access command fields rather than information of their own.
The buffered address only selects which information word is returned during the access (lines 162 and 168), making it a held address copy rather than a separate conceptual asset.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus response handshake and error status
considered, not kept.reason: The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error flag is tied to a constant (lines 160 and 169-170), so the handshake-copy and constant-status rules exclude them.

considered, not kept.concept: Clock, reset and access timing state
considered, not kept.reason: The clock and reset only time or initialize assignments, while the access buffering only retimes the transaction (lines 89-97 and 154-164), so the clock/reset and pacing rules exclude this state.

reply keys: the 2026-10-13 format as written in 'raw'; 'reply' holds it in v5 keys
